companyDescription: Autonomous Delivery Robotics · Sidewalk delivery robots for food & laundry across 44 cities — building the last-mile autonomous logistics network of the future powered by Nvidia edge AI
priceNote: Small-cap robotics consolidating ~$7.75 — analyst avg target $18.45 implies +138% upside; Q2 earnings projected Aug 6
summary: Serve Robotics is the purest autonomous delivery robotics play in the public market — 2,000+ robots deployed in 44 cities across 14 states with Uber Eats and DoorDash integration. Q1 2026 revenue $3M (+578% YoY), 2026 guidance $26M. 9 analysts with Strong Buy consensus and average target $17-18 (140%+ upside). New partnerships: NoScrubs laundry delivery expanding beyond food. Unveiled 'Maggie' AI conversational robot at Nvidia GTC 2026. Ultra-speculative: tiny revenues, not yet profitable, but the physical AI infrastructure story is compelling if robotics adoption accelerates.

catalysts.name: Q2 2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: Projected Aug 6, 2026 (not yet confirmed). Q1 revenue $3M (+578% YoY) beat; FY2026 guide $26M requires H2 acceleration. Watch fleet count, city expansion, and Diligent Robotics integration update.

catalysts.name: Fleet Scale to 5,000+ Robots
catalysts.description: Serve has deployed 2,000 robots across 44 cities and 14 states. Scaling to 5,000+ robots targets breakeven on unit economics. Each robot serves Uber Eats, DoorDash, Shake Shack, Little Caesars — per-robot revenue growing as utilization increases.

catalysts.name: NoScrubs Laundry — Expansion Beyond Food
catalysts.description: June 2026: Serve launched laundry delivery with NoScrubs in Los Angeles — first non-food delivery vertical. Diversification from food delivery reduces Uber Eats concentration risk and expands TAM for sidewalk robots.

catalysts.name: Maggie AI Robot at Nvidia GTC
catalysts.description: Unveiled 'Maggie' — AI conversational robot built on T-Mobile 5G Advanced + Nvidia edge computing at GTC 2026. Demonstrates SERV is not just a hardware company but an AI+5G robotics platform.

risks: Revenue too small — $26M 2026 guidance for a $280M market cap = 10x P/S; needs massive scaling to justify valuation
Not yet profitable — non-GAAP operating expenses $160-170M vs $26M revenue = massive cash burn
Uber Eats / DoorDash concentration risk — losing a platform partner destroys the business model
Regulatory risk — city permit requirements, sidewalk navigation laws can slow or block deployment
Competition from Amazon Scout (restarted), Starship Technologies, Nuro — well-funded rivals

estimateDates.note: Revenue run-rate read — $26M FY guide requires strong H2
Key scale milestone for unit economics

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Higher rates increase cost of capital for unprofitable small-cap growth companies — SERV's cash burn is rate-sensitive for future financing rounds
macroRisk.inflationNote: Robot hardware and maintenance costs face supply chain inflation. Labor savings thesis gets STRONGER with higher wages (robots replace human delivery at lower cost).
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Physical AI (robotics) sector attracts investor interest regardless of rate environment. But SERV specifically needs low rates to fund its cash burn runway without dilutive raises.
macroRisk.summary: Fed risk MEDIUM — SERV is unprofitable with $160-170M annual opex vs $26M revenue. Lower rates reduce dilution risk. The labor replacement thesis actually strengthens with wage inflation. Main risk is runway, not macro.
